value.question: Can a crystal foundation model fine-tuned on a transport proxy generate Li-ion solid electrolytes with higher conductivity than unconditioned generation or database screening?
value.hypothesis: Conditioning MatterGen's adapter on predicted ionic conductivity gives low-barrier candidates at higher hit rate than screening; transport labels are scarce but learnable.

compute_axis.quantity: generated candidate crystal structures screened per arm

held_fixed: fine-tuned MatterGen checkpoint and conductivity predictor
equal candidate counts across arms at each level

predictions.if_lever: Scaling candidates to 100,000 makes the conditioned generator's hit-rate advantage over both baselines significant; at 1,000 it is within noise.
predictions.if_not: Scaling candidates does not separate conditioned from baseline hit rates; the gap stays within seed noise at every level, so fine-tuning adds nothing.
predictions.decision_rule: At 100k candidates per arm, the conditioned arm's hit rate (predicted log10 sigma >= -4 S/cm) must exceed both baselines by >=2x, and its top-10 median CHGNet-NEB barrier be >=0.1 eV below the best baseline's; otherwise if_not.
predictions.noise_rule: Three generation seeds per arm; 95% bootstrap confidence interval on hit rate; a real gap is one whose CI exceeds 2x the maximum within-arm seed spread.
predictions.expected_why: Conditioned generation has repeatedly beaten screening (MatterGen, Ferrogen's 80x), and the conductivity proxy is learnable (MCC 0.63).

value.compute_tested_why: The test varies the number of generated candidates (the quantity parallel GPUs buy: 1k/10k/100k) and measures whether the conditioned-vs-baseline hit-rate gap emerges above noise; the fine-tuning method is held fixed across levels.
value.scored_against: Each arm's top-candidate predicted log10 sigma and CHGNet-NEB/DFT-NEB migration barriers, compared with the npj 403-conductor median (-4.41 log10 S/cm) and published NEB barriers (LiTi2(PO4)3 0.41 eV, LATP 0.19 eV).

arms.what: MatterGen fine-tuned on the transport proxy, classifier-free guided sampling toward high log10 sigma
Unconditioned MatterGen base samples, screened by the same conductivity predictor
Exhaustive screening of the 6,972 Li-containing ICSD compositions by the predictor

baseline.what: Arm B (unconditioned MatterGen) and arm C (exhaustive ICSD screening), both ranked by the same conductivity predictor.

anchor.what: Reproduce MatterGen's 38.57% S.U.N. and 0.021 Angstrom RMSD on 1,024 samples; reproduce the npj predictor's 0.85 log10 sigma MAE.
anchor.tolerance: S.U.N. within +/-3 percentage points; RMSD <= 0.1 Angstrom; predictor MAE within +/-0.1 log10 sigma.
anchor.independent_code: Released microsoft/mattergen checkpoint and evaluation script; npj CrabNet composition model re-implemented in scikit-learn.

checks: Released checkpoint S.U.N. rate within +/-3 points of 38.57% and RMSD <= 0.1 Angstrom
Predictor 5-fold MAE within +/-0.1 of the published 0.85 log10 sigma on the 403 compositions
CHGNet-NEB for LiTi2(PO4)3 within 0.1 eV of the published 0.41 eV
Generated structures charge-neutral, <=20 atoms/primitive cell, DFT-relaxable, novel vs the training set

phases.what: Fetch mattergen_base checkpoint and npj dataset; map 403 compositions to ICSD/MP structures; anchor the S.U.N. rate.
phases.stop_rule: abort if the S.U.N. anchor fails tolerance

phases.what: Train composition conductivity regressor/classifier; anchor held-out MAE.

gate.else: fall back to classifier-only conditioning on P(log10 sigma >= -4) as the label

phases.what: Fine-tune MatterGen adapter on predicted log10 sigma (time-boxed).
phases.stop_rule: stop when validation loss plateaus or 24h elapse

phases.what: Generate and screen arms A/B at 1k/10k/100k and arm C; measure hit rates.
phases.stop_rule: stop after all levels complete or the generation line budget is spent

phases.what: CHGNet-NEB on top-50, then DFT-NEB on top-10.

gate.else: skip DFT-NEB and report CHGNet-NEB only (conditioning failed to yield low-barrier candidates)

numbers.name: Published regression MAE
numbers.quote: The best regression models achieve a mean absolute error for log10(sigma) of 0.85, and the best classification models have a Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) of 0.63, assessed under k-folds cross-validation in both cases.

numbers.name: Published classifier MCC
numbers.quote: The best regression models achieve a mean absolute error for log10(sigma) of 0.85, and the best classification models have a Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) of 0.63, assessed under k-folds cross-validation in both cases.

numbers.name: Median known-conductor conductivity
numbers.quote: The room temperature conductivities span the range of 5.00 x 10^-16 to 2.50 x 10^-2 S cm-1, with a mean log10(sigma) of -5.01 and median of -4.41.

numbers.name: High-conductivity screen threshold
numbers.quote: We develop supervised regression and classification models to predict the lithium ion conductivity and assess whether a material will possess an ionic conductivity log10(sigma) >= 4 at room temperature, where the conductivity is reported in units of S cm-1.

numbers.name: LiTi2(PO4)3 vacancy barrier

numbers.name: LATP interstitial barrier
numbers.quote: DFT-based NEB calculations have revealed that Li ions migrate following a vacancy mechanism with a barrier of about 0.41 eV in pure LiTi2(PO4)3, while the interstitial mechanism with a lower calculated barrier of 0.19 eV occurs in the LATP structure.
